authorityBoundary: Computing owns only synthesis and this research contract. Host/Harness/Runtime/World/domain repositories retain native facts. Provider results are experimental Agent observations, not product truth.

budget.note: Retries increase physical Provider call count but not accepted semantic-decision target.

candidate: No representation is presumed to survive. The preferred final candidate is the smallest treatment within 1 percentage point of the best EX7 action accuracy with no additional critical unsafe errors, conditional on prior-stage non-inferiority and intervention/transfer evidence.
deletionOrNoChangeOutcome: A valid final result may be compact prose alone, compact prose plus a question grammar, or no universal representation at all. Typed relation notation remains research-local unless it earns causal action value beyond prose.
evidenceSelection: Seventeen responsibility families were selected from current owner-native Host/Harness/Runtime/World/Finance/Security/Game/Human/Studio/Web evidence before any live EX3 call. Each family has five pre-frozen independent surfaces A-E; later stages may not rewrite an oracle after seeing earlier results.
independentOracle: Owner-native current repositories observed before live calls define the action oracle. Computing freezes only the experiment-local questions/options; it does not become product authority.
invalidityConditions: Change any oracleDecision or criticalUnsafeOptions after the first live Provider call.
Reuse EX3 A-surface wording as EX4 B evidence or tune B after observing A results.
Treat an improvement on EX4 representation labels as ontology validity without EX5 intervention and EX6 drift transfer.
Treat Agent-observer performance as human comprehension.
Count transport/schema failures as semantic wrong answers; physical calls remain cost evidence and accepted semantic trials remain separately reported.
Post-hoc exclude difficult families to satisfy a gate.
Promote a service/schema/ontology merely because a benchmark treatment wins.
mission: Falsify whether Ordivon needs any explanation structure beyond strong compact owner-native responsibility prose, then test causal intervention, drift transfer, and final minimum compression without promoting a closed ontology.
negativeControl: Project-name shortcuts are removed in EX6; EX7 uses the untouched E surface. Wrong choices explicitly include common unsafe inferences such as local execution=>external effect, persistence=>semantic ownership, Run=>domain completion, target=>current product, Agent observer=>human comprehension, and capability=>authority.
publicationBoundary: Do not build ExplanationService, RelationGraphService, ontology server, universal primaryOwner record, mandatory reasoning ceremony, global truth/currentness database, or presentation authority from these experiments. Studio/Web may later consume the final factual claims as expression/publication inputs without owning them.
questionOrHypothesis: EX3 discovers materially wrong actions under strong compact prose. EX4 asks whether any representation repairs those failures on pre-frozen parallel cases. EX5 asks whether the smallest candidate improves deletion/intervention consequence prediction. EX6 asks whether it transfers to de-identified unfamiliar systems without project-name shortcuts. EX7 selects the smallest non-inferior final explanation grammar on an untouched surface.
stopRule: EX3 declares an explanation deficit if compact action accuracy is below 97.5% OR any family repeats a critical unsafe option in at least 2/6 replicates. EX4 promotion requires >=3 percentage-point gain on EX3-deficit families, elimination of repeated critical errors, and <=1 point overall regression. EX5/EX6 must be non-inferior to compact within 1 point and add no critical unsafe errors. EX7 selects the smallest candidate within 1 point of the best treatment with no extra critical unsafe errors; if compact prose already satisfies this, delete the extra structure.
strongBaseline: Strong compact natural-language responsibility explanation that already states the owner-native causal law without typed relation jargon. EX4 compares exact-question scaffold, typed relation notation, and a causal card against that baseline. EX5/EX6 compare compact prose with the seven-question grammar. EX7 compares compact prose, seven-question grammar, four-question compression, and typed notation.
